**Research summary**

Apple's fiscal 2024 fourth quarter (ended September 28, 2024), reported October 31, 2024, showed quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year — the strongest growth rate in several quarters, driven by Services and a stabilizing iPhone cycle plus the Apple Intelligence rollout. For the full fiscal year, total net sales were $391.0 billion ($391,035 million) and **net income was $93.7 billion ($93,736 million)**, or $6.08 per diluted share — down from $96,995 million the prior year because FY2024 absorbed a one-time $10.2 billion European tax charge (operating income actually rose to $123.2 billion). Growth on the top line, expanding Services mix, and a roughly 30% net margin despite the tax hit made this a constructive setup rather than a deteriorating one, so I judged AAPL worth adding to a portfolio that currently holds only MSFT.

**What I did**

I bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75, which filled at $222.75 for a total of $9,801.00 — under the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily cap, with cash covered entirely from the $50,000 already in the account (no transfers or withdrawals). The limit was set at the prevailing ask ($222.72, last trade $222.70), so it stayed close to market as the mandate requires. The trade is a buy of a permitted ticker and leaves me $10,199 of today's allowance unused. Key figures relied on, all confirmed against Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K filed 2024-11-01 and cross-checked against the Q4 earnings release: net income $93,736 million, revenue $391,035 million, diluted EPS $6.08.
